title: Compatibility Plugin - Bifrost
text:
Open Source Features
Compatibility Plugin

Request and response transformations for LiteLLM proxy/SDK compatibility.

​
Compatibility Transformations
The LiteLLM compatibility plugin provides two transformations:
Text-to-Chat Conversion - Automatically converts text completion requests to chat completion format for models that only support chat APIs
Chat-to-Responses Conversion - Automatically converts chat completion requests to responses format for models that only support responses APIs
Drop Unsupported Params - Automatically drops unsupported parameters if the model doesn’t support them. A reasoning.summary value the datasheet marks unsupported (supports_reasoning_summary_detailed, supports_reasoning_summary_concise or supports_reasoning_summary_auto set to false) becomes auto when the model accepts auto, and is dropped otherwise. Reasoning effort is always kept
Unsupported Parameter Conversion - Automatically converts unsupported parameters to their supported equivalents
Reasoning-Only Models to Responses - Routes chat completion requests to the Responses API for models that cannot reason alongside tool calls on chat completions
Decision-to-Responses Emulation - Answers decision requests for models without a native decisions endpoint by prompting the model through the Responses API (off by default)
When either transformation is applied, responses include extra_fields.converted_request_type: <transformed_request_type>. If request parameters are dropped, the keys are added in extra_fields.dropped_compat_plugin_params.
​
1. Text-to-Chat Conversion
Many modern AI models (like GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4, Claude, etc.) only support the chat completion API and don’t have native text completion endpoints. LiteLLM compatibility mode automatically handles this by:
Checking if the model supports text completion natively (using the model catalog)
If not supported, converting your text prompt to chat message format
Calling the chat completion endpoint internally
Transforming the response back to text completion format
Returning content in choices[0].text instead of choices[0].message.content
Smart Conversion: The conversion only happens when the model doesn’t support text completions natively. If a model has native text completion support (like OpenAI’s davinci models), Bifrost uses the text completion endpoint directly without any conversion.
This allows you to use a unified text completion interface across all providers, even those that only support chat completions.
​

Request Transformation:
Your text prompt becomes a user message: {"role": "user", "content": "your prompt"}
Parameters like max_tokens, temperature, top_p are mapped to chat equivalents
Fallbacks are preserved
Response Transformation:
choices[0].message.content → choices[0].text
object: "chat.completion" → object: "text_completion"
Usage statistics and metadata are preserved
​
2. Chat-to-Responses Conversion
Some AI models (like OpenAI o1-pro) only support the responses API and don’t support native chat completion endpoints. LiteLLM compatibility mode automatically handles this by:
Checking if the model supports chat completion natively (using the model catalog)
If not supported, converting your chat message to responses API format
Calling the responses endpoint internally
Transforming the response back to chat completion format
Smart Conversion: The conversion only happens when the model doesn’t support chat completions natively. If a model has native chat completion support (like OpenAI’s gpt-4 models), Bifrost uses the chat completion endpoint directly without any conversion.
This allows you to use a unified chat completion interface across all providers, even those that only support responses API.
​

​
3. Reasoning-Only Models to Responses
Some models (for example several GPT-5 series models) do not support reasoning together with tool calls on the chat completions API. Their datasheet entry sets supports_reasoning_with_tool_calls: false. For any chat completion request on such a model, with or without tools, Bifrost:
Calls the Responses API instead, where reasoning and tools work together
Transforms the response back to chat completion format
With force_reasoning_only_models_to_responses off, the request stays on chat completions. What happens to reasoning then depends on should_drop_params:
should_drop_params on: when the request carries tools, reasoning is turned off (dropped, or set to none when the model supports it).
should_drop_params off: the request is sent with its reasoning setting unchanged.
Controlled by force_reasoning_only_models_to_responses (on by default).
​
4. Decision-to-Responses Emulation
Decision requests (/v1/decisions, /openai/v1/decisions, /typesafe/v1/systemone) are served natively only by decision models. With this setting off, a decision request for any other model, such as openai/gpt-4o, fails with HTTP 400 and code unsupported_operation:
decisions is not supported by openai provider

With convert_decision_to_responses on, Bifrost instead:
Checks whether the model is a native decisions model: its supports_decisions datasheet entry, or without one the models Bifrost recognizes by name:
OpenAI’s gpt-6-luna family on openai and azure (another provider hosting it, such as OpenRouter, serves it as a chat model)
Typesafe’s typesafe/ models, and every model on the typesafe provider
clef models (clef, clef-flash, clef-omni, by bare name or @cf/cloudflare/ ID) on cloudflare
pplx-decider-* on perplexity
nimble, tev1, clef, clef-flash, and laya (any tag) on ollama
Microsoft-Decision-1 on azure
ai_decide and System One models (system.ai.openjev-* and system.ai.typesafeai-jev-*) on databricks
If it is, calls the provider’s decisions endpoint without any conversion
If not, encodes the questions as a forced function tool, sends the input to the model’s Responses API, and maps the call’s arguments back to typed answers
Why it breaks custom providers. The check relies on the model catalog, which has no entries for custom providers. With the setting on, a custom provider serving decisions, such as Laya or Nimble on the Typesafe base format, or gpt-6-luna behind a custom provider on the OpenAI base format, is emulated through a Responses API it may not serve instead of answered natively. This applies to Complexity Router classification too.
We recommend keeping this setting off and sending decisions to a model that serves them natively. An emulated answer is a chat model’s guess, not a calibrated judgment, and it costs a full chat call.
Behavior notes:
The check runs on every attempt, fallbacks included.
An emulated response reports extra_fields.converted_request_type: "responses" and is billed as the chat call it is.
A request with an image or other non-text part is rejected, as are passthrough extra params (x-bf-passthrough-extra-params).
Per request, the header x-bf-compat: ["convert_decision_to_responses"] turns it on for that request only.
In the Go SDK, it is on when the compat plugin is registered with compat.Config{ConvertDecisionToResponses: true}.
​
Enabling LiteLLM Compatibility
Gateway UI
Configuration File
Open the Bifrost dashboard
Navigate to Settings → Compatibility
There you can enable the features you need:
Convert Text to Chat - converts text completion requests to chat for models that only support chat
Convert Chat to Responses - converts chat completion requests to responses for models that only support responses
Drop Unsupported Params - drops unsupported parameters based on model catalog allowlist
Convert Unsupported Params Values - converts parameter values the model cannot accept, such as a token cap above the model limit, to values it can. See the list of supported parameters below.
Azure DeepSeek - converts Azure DeepSeek responses requests to chat completions so reasoning is preserved for coding harnesses
Reasoning-only models to Responses - routes chat completion requests to the Responses API for models that cannot reason with tool calls on chat completions
Emulate Decisions API on non-decision models - answers decision requests for models without a native decisions endpoint through the Responses API
Save your configuration
​
Supported Parameters
The following parameter values are converted to values the model accepts:
Parameter	Original Value	Transformed Value	Provider
max_completion_tokens / max_tokens (chat), max_output_tokens (responses), max_tokens (text)	Above the model’s max_output_tokens	The model’s max_output_tokens	Every model with a known output limit
Same as above	Below the model’s min_output_tokens	The model’s min_output_tokens	Models whose catalog row sets min_output_tokens
reasoning.max_tokens	Sent with a token cap that was lowered	Scaled by the same ratio as the cap	Every model with a known output limit
reasoning.max_tokens	Outside the model’s thinking-budget range	The nearest end of the range	Claude, Gemini 2.5, and models whose catalog row sets reasoning_budget
reasoning.max_tokens	At or above the lowered cap, or the model’s max_output_tokens when no cap was sent	One below that cap	Every model with a known output limit
Limits come from the model catalog, with built-in fallbacks for Claude output limits and Claude and Gemini 2.5 thinking budgets. Only values present in the request are changed; none are added. Budgets of 0 and -1 are left as sent. The conversion runs again for each fallback, so every fallback model is fitted to its own limits. Each conversion is logged as a warning on the request, for example max_output_tokens: 1000000 -> 65536.
developer role messages are mapped to system by the Gemini, Vertex and Bedrock providers themselves, so that works without this setting.
Namespace-scoped tools are no longer handled by this plugin. Bifrost core flattens them for every provider whose wire does not support the namespace tool type, renames each nested function to <namespace>__<function> so names stay unique, and maps returned function_call items back to the original name plus namespace.
​
Supported Providers
Text completion to chat completion conversion works with any provider that supports chat completions but lacks native text completion support:
Provider	Native Text Completion	With Fallback
OpenAI (GPT-4, GPT-3.5-turbo)	No	Yes
Anthropic (Claude)	No	Yes
Groq	No	Yes
Gemini	No	Yes
Mistral	No	Yes
Bedrock	Varies by model	Yes
Chat completion to responses conversion works with any provider that supports responses but lacks native chat completion support:
Provider	Native Chat Completion	With Fallback
OpenAI (o1-pro)	No	Yes
​
Behavior Details
Model Capability Detection:
Bifrost uses the model catalog to check if a model supports text completion
If the model has a “completion” mode in its pricing data, it supports text completion
Conversion only happens when the model lacks native text completion support
​
Transformations Reference
​
Transformation 1: Text-to-Chat Conversion
Applies to: Text completion requests on chat-only models
Phase	Original	Transformed
Request	Text prompt (string)	Chat message with role: "user"
Request	Array prompts	Concatenated into text content blocks
Request	text_completion request type	chat_completion request type
Request	max_tokens, temperature, top_p	Mapped to chat equivalents
Response	choices[0].message.content	choices[0].text
Response	object: "chat.completion"	object: "text_completion"
​
Transformation 2: Chat-to-Responses Conversion
Applies to: Chat completion requests on responses-only models
Phase	Original	Transformed
Request	Chat message with role: "user"	Responses input with role: "user"
Request	chat_completion request type	responses request type
​
Metadata Set on Transformed Responses
When either transformation is applied:
extra_fields.request_type: Reflects the original request type
extra_fields.original_model_requested: The originally requested model
extra_fields.resolved_model_used: The actual provider API identifier used (equals original_model_requested when no alias mapping exists)
​
Error Handling
When errors occur on transformed requests:
Original request type and model are preserved in error metadata
extra_fields.converted_request_type: Set to type of request that was converted to (i.e., chat_completion or responses)
extra_fields.provider: The provider that handled the request
extra_fields.original_model_requested: The originally requested model
extra_fields.dropped_compat_plugin_params: If any unsupported parameters were dropped, the keys are added here
​
Header Overrides
To enable compat plugins per request, you can use x-bf-compat header:
When x-bf-compat: true or x-bf-compat: ["*"], enables all compat plugins options
When x-bf-compat: ["<setting1>","<setting2>"], enables the specified settings (available settings: convert_text_to_chat, convert_chat_to_responses, should_drop_params, should_convert_params, azure_deepseek, force_reasoning_only_models_to_responses, convert_decision_to_responses)
​
What’s Preserved
Model selection and fallback chain
Temperature, top_p, max_tokens, and other generation parameters
Stop sequences and frequency/presence penalties
Usage statistics and token counts
​
When to Use This
Good Use Cases:
Migrating from LiteLLM to Bifrost without code changes
Maintaining backward compatibility with text completion interfaces or chat completion interfaces
Using a unified API across providers with different capabilities
Consider Alternatives When:
You need chat-specific features (system messages, conversation history)
You want explicit control over message formatting
Performance is critical (direct chat requests avoid conversion overhead)
​
Related Features
Fallbacks - Automatic provider failover
Drop-in Replacement - Use existing SDKs with Bifrost
LiteLLM Integration - Using LiteLLM SDK with Bifrost
